evidence.methodology_notes: Per language_quality.md, dependency-manager package-corpus maturity and realized CI/platform breadth belong to Ecosystem, not Language Quality; excluded here. Only assigned language (Quidra) and assigned requirement IDs scored in this shard.

metric.dependency_simplicity.normalization_rationale: Scored on minimal external tooling for dependency resolution, absence of arbitrary code execution during install, simplicity of version constraint language, completeness/transparency of dependency graph via lockfile, and protection against manifest drift. Quidra scores well above median due to no install-time scripts, flat conjunctive version ranges, and a hashed two-identity lockfile covering the whole transitive closure. Points deducted for reliance on external processes (git, curl/tar) and no documented compiled/binary dependency-graph caching.
raw_observations: Quidra packages are plain source packages with a single main.qui entrypoint; released packages add a quidra.package manifest (docs/packages.md).
Install only from immutable vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release tags, never from moving branches; an explicit version must exist as an exact tag or install fails (docs/packages.md).
No install script execution, eliminating a class of transitive build-time side effects common in npm/pip/cargo ecosystems.
Version ranges are simple conjunctive SemVer terms (=,<,<=,>,>=); lockfile format upgrades (v1->v2->v3) remain backward-readable.
quidra.lock records distribution and import identity plus a content SHA-256 hash per package, covering the full transitive import graph deterministically in one flat file.
Asset-backed installs add an opt-in second dependency vector requiring curl and tar; installer inspects archives and rejects path traversal or replacement of protected files.
quidra.package recognizes a closed key set; an unknown key is a hard error, preventing manifest-format drift. Supplementary metadata lives in optional project.toml.
requires.quidra is mandatory for released packages; requires.abi is a separate exact-match field rather than a range.
Remote installation requires git as an external tool, and asset installs require curl/tar.

metric.portability_design_platform_neutr.normalization_rationale: Scored on whether platform variability is modeled as declarative data vs scattered conditionals, first-class multi-platform package-artifact support, multi-OS/compiler toolchain design intent, and evidence of a genuine compiler-level cross-compilation/target abstraction (distinct from realized CI breadth, which is Ecosystem). Quidra shows strong declarative centralization and a clean per-platform asset mechanism. It scores below a language with an explicit mature cross-compilation target model because available docs show only CI-level OS coverage, not compiler target abstraction.
raw_observations: project.toml is the single source of truth for supported operating systems/targets and the backend id/display/kind table, i.e. platform support is declared data rather than scattered ifdef logic (docs/development.md).
Release checks require Linux, macOS, and Windows CI plus GCC and Clang release builds, indicating the reference toolchain targets multi-OS, multi-compiler portability from the outset.

Packages declare platform-specific optional binary assets via asset.<platform> keys with an asset.default fallback, giving the package format first-class declarative multi-platform artifact support (docs/packages.md).
Backend design is an id/display/kind table driven from project.toml, implying device/target backends are modeled uniformly.
Version/ABI/IR/package-schema numbers are centrally tracked in project.toml and mechanically checked for consistency, supporting platform-neutral tooling.

No evidence in readable docs of a formalized target-triple/cross-compilation model comparable to Go's GOOS/GOARCH or Zig's cross-compilation-by-default; documented breadth is at CI-matrix level (an Ecosystem concern) rather than compiler-level target abstraction.
